title: Investigation into the impact of renal denervation on microvascular function in uncontrolled hypertension: a prospective observational study.
summary:
This prospective observational study investigates the impact of renal denervation on vascular health in patients with uncontrolled arterial hypertension, as well as the temporal dynamics of blood pressure changes during the observation period using telemonitoring (home monitoring). Renal denervation is a minimally invasive, catheter-based procedure in which sympathetic nerve fibers within the renal artery walls are ablated using ultrasound.

Decisions regarding the indication for and performance of the renal denervation procedure are made clinically. Following participant enrollment and initial assessment, home blood pressure readings are monitored via telemedicine for one month. Subsequently, following the renal denervation procedure, home blood pressure readings are monitored via telemedicine for 12 months. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Uncontrolled arterial hypertension with a clinical indication for renal denervation
Optional: MRI compatibility (no tinnitus, no tattoos, no magnetic implants)
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Clinically significant and uncontrolled supraventricular or ventricular cardiac arrhythmias (excluding adequately rate-controlled atrial fibrillation)
2.	Severe valvular heart disease and/or valvular disease requiring intervention
3.	History of significant neurological or psychiatric disorders (e.g., seizure disorders, severe traumatic brain injury, depression, schizophrenia, dementia)
4.	Malignancies limiting life expectancy
5.	Intolerance to ASA (acetylsalicylic acid)
6.	Impaired renal function (GFR <40 ml/min/1.73 m²)
7.	Renal artery stenosis
8.	Untreated secondary causes of hypertension
9.	Severe aortic atherosclerosis
